implemented_capabilities.capability: Cloud access-path investigation (identity -> session -> workload -> role -> role -> critical data asset)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Fixed-shape, parameterised read-only Cypher (ro_query) over five relationship types. Distinguishes path_found / no_path / unknown entity / invalid_input / query_error explicitly. Paths are fixed-arity patterns, not generic traversal.

MATCH p=(s)-[*1..6]->(t) with an all() filter on allowed rel types and non-blocked sessions, ORDER BY hop_count LIMIT 1. This enumerates every path up to 6 hops and then sorts, rather than using a shortest-path algorithm, so it will not scale; the code says it is the portable fallback because graph algorithm procedures differ between FalkorDB installs.

Sets route.containment_status='BLOCKED' on one synthetic HAS_SESSION edge (idempotent) and then re-queries remaining active paths to report alternative_path_remains vs no_qualifying_path_in_modeled_graph. Requires confirmed=true. Action history is an in-process list lost on restart. Only 'primary'/'alternate' route ids are accepted.

Rule 'demo-rules-v1': +35 base, +30 public workload, +30 EXCESSIVE flag, small increments for extra paths, capped at 100. Self-described as demonstration logic; not a computed risk model. The 'EXCESSIVE' classification is a pre-seeded edge property, not evaluated.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Gemini + MCP grounded explanation with fallback
implemented_capabilities.notes: Spawns the MCP server over stdio and lets Gemini call 5 read-only tools; _ground_answer rejects model text that names unknown entity ids, relationship types, a different risk score, or claims containment while paths remain, and falls back to a canonical summary. The grounding check is regex-based and heuristic (ids must contain a hyphen/underscore and a digit). Requires a Gemini API key; otherwise the endpoint returns 503.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Synthetic graph seeding and four scripted scenarios
implemented_capabilities.notes: Alerts BH-1042, BH-IAM-2001, BH-WORKLOAD-3001, BH-CONTAINMENT-4001 are a hard-coded 4-entry catalog mapped to fixed target ids; the data is a ~27-node synthetic graph (README). No ingestion of real cloud data.

graph_models_and_cypher: Labels: Identity, Session, Workload, IAMRole, DataAsset. Edges: HAS_SESSION{route_id, containment_status}, CAN_ACCESS, RUNS_AS, CAN_ASSUME{assessment, granted_actions, granted_resource_scope, intended_scope, reason}, CAN_READ. Cypher: fixed-arity path matches returning list comprehensions of nodes(p)/relationships(p); one variable-length [*1..6] with all(rel IN relationships(p) WHERE type(rel) IN [...]); SET on a single relationship property for containment. All reads via ro_query, parameters only. No APOC/GDS. Graph name via FALKORDB_GRAPH_NAME (default 'blastshield').
algorithms: Fixed-pattern attack-path matching with property filters (queries.py)
Bounded depth-6 path enumeration with relationship-type allowlist and blocked-edge exclusion (queries.py:FIND_SHORTEST_ACCESS_PATH_QUERY)
Containment verification by re-running reachability after a state change (integration.py:simulate_containment)
LLM-output grounding validation by id/relationship/score cross-check (gemini_service.py:_ground_answer)
backend_interfaces: FastAPI: GET /api/health, GET /api/alerts, POST /api/investigations, POST /api/agent/investigate, GET /api/containment/{alert_id}, POST /api/containment/simulate, GET /api/containment/{alert_id}/history
MCP stdio server backend/app/mcp/server.py (uses mcp.server.MCPServer): investigate_alert, find_shortest_access_path, get_blast_radius, get_containment_route_statuses, get_tool_trace
frontend_interfaces: React single-file dashboard frontend/src/App.jsx (alert picker, outcome badge, path/evidence view, risk breakdown, MCP trace, containment simulator with confirmation)
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: One-shot Gemini tool-calling session over MCP with a per-process TOOL_TRACE (last 30 calls) and a stored CANONICAL_INVESTIGATION used for grounding. No persistent memory, no approval workflow beyond a confirmed=true boolean on the containment request.
tests_present: backend/tests/test_integration.py (17 test functions, unittest, mock-based) and backend/tests/test_live_falkordb.py (4 tests needing a live FalkorDB); plus test_falkordb_connection.py (connectivity script). The mock source file mock_graph_service.py is absent; only a compiled mock_graph_service.cpython-311.pyc is committed.
dependency_requirements: mcp (unpinned; code imports mcp.server.MCPServer which is not the mcp 1.x FastMCP API used by the other repos in this batch)
security_findings: backend/app/agent/__pycache__/*.pyc, backend/app/__pycache__/*.pyc and backend/tests/__pycache__ - compiled bytecode committed to the repository, including mock_graph_service.cpython-311.pyc whose source is not present; do not import or execute it, delete before merging

backend/app/main.py:73-99 - /api/agent/investigate spawns a Python subprocess MCP server (sys.executable -m app.mcp.server) and sends data to the Gemini API; child env copies the full process environment including GEMINI_API_KEY and any other secrets
backend/app/agent/gemini_service.py:153 - prints the model name to stdout; no key logged. The key is read from environment/.env (not committed)
backend/app/main.py:24-30 - CORS limited to localhost:5173 with allow_credentials=True (reasonable); no authentication on any route, including POST /api/containment/simulate which mutates the graph

backend/app/graph/queries.py:243-249 - unbounded path enumeration [*1..6] can be made expensive by a caller choosing well-connected source/target ids (DoS risk), though ids are length-limited to 128 characters and parameterised
backend/app/graph/connection.py:19 - FalkorDB connection has no password/TLS option; unauthenticated Redis-protocol connection
backend/app/mcp/server.py:20-21 - module-level mutable TOOL_TRACE and CANONICAL_INVESTIGATION shared across calls (not safe for concurrent sessions)
No hard-coded secrets, eval/exec or pickle found in the source files.
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps attack-path/identity-to-data reachability (ThreatPath, exploit-path, ExploitReach, other security repos), blast radius of exposed workloads, and simulated containment. Its distinguishing piece is the LLM grounding validator and re-verification after containment.
evidence_drift_relevance: LOW - provenance block (dataset_version, coverage, updated_at), canonical-vs-model grounding and post-action re-verification are useful patterns, but there is no temporal validity, supersession, invalidation or real approval workflow.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: A small guard that rejects LLM explanations containing entities, relationships or scores not present in the canonical graph result, and a before/after re-query verification of a state-changing action; both are pattern-reusable for Kairos agents without copying the cloud-IAM domain.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB; Gemini API key and an MCP 2.x-style server only for the agent path

strategy_rationale: The domain logic is a four-scenario synthetic demo with fixed patterns and a stub risk score, and the security space is already covered by the more complete ThreatPath. Borrow the grounding validator and re-verification pattern as reference.
